quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A downgrade or hill is coming.
Road construction ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: A downgrade or hill is coming.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep or long hill is ahead. The road may have sharp curves too.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: Intersections ahead.
Road construction.
A curve in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about dangers ahead. This sign warns of a curve to the right.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light bounces back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles may not see you.
Cars behind you may follow too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light bounces back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beams reflect back at you and reduce your visibility.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see better around the sides of the vehicle.
Other drivers tend to cut in before passing large vehicles.
Staying too close puts you in the vehicle's air draft.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see better around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicle drivers cannot see you if you drive directly behind them. Keep extra distance so you can see around the truck or bus and see the road ahead.

questions.question: If a car passes you in a no passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and stay in your lane.
Slow down so the other car can return safely to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other car can return safely to your lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down to help the passing vehicle return to the lane safely. This protects everyone from dangers ahead.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting the interstate?

options.text: About halfway down the exit lane.
As you reach the exit lane.
Right when you enter the exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Stay at interstate speed until you enter the exit lane. Then slow to the speed posted on the exit ramp.

questions.question: Which statement about medications and driving is true?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs are safe for driving if you take the right dose.
Any medicine prescribed by a doctor is safe to take anytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications—prescription or over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines often cause drowsiness. Know how your medication affects you before driving.

questions.question: How can you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Change lanes.
Keep your speed and lane the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes.
questions.explanation: Move to another lane if you can to let entering vehicles merge safely. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to help them merge smoothly.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross it to pass when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic flows both ways.
The road direction is changing.
School zone with a crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows both ways.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a road with traffic going both directions.

questions.question: At an intersection where you cannot see clearly to the side, you should:

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.
questions.explanation: Stop at the intersection. Move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions before proceeding.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes in an intersection. Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Watch for other drivers trying to enter the same lane.

questions.question: An orange and red triangular sign on a vehicle always means:

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Road work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles display an orange and red triangle on the back. These include farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and animal-drawn carts.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road will change direction or become narrower ahead.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will change direction or become narrower ahead.
questions.explanation: This warning sign alerts you to a change in road direction or a narrower road ahead. You may see these signs at sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: To avoid glare from oncoming headlights:

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep looking at the centerline.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then continue looking ahead to track the oncoming vehicle's position.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for bicycles, animals, and pedestrians that may cross the road.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road widens ahead.
The right lane will end soon. Move to the left lane.
Highway entrance ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane will end soon. Move to the left lane.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you that one lane is ending. Traffic must merge to the left.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you another road crosses the highway ahead. Be prepared to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance at night because it is harder to see. Use your headlights correctly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights as this causes glare blindness.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Move into another lane while in an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane while in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Watch for other drivers trying to enter your lane.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left, as long as no traffic is coming toward you. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels leave the road. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back on the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, hold the steering wheel firmly, take your foot off the gas, and gently brake. Once you slow down, check traffic and find a safe place to return to the road. Jerking the steering wheel can make you lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire suddenly goes flat?

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while driving, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down by releasing the gas and using the brakes lightly.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause more severe crashes and longer stopping distances. As speed increases, the chance of serious injury and death increases. Keep more distance between you and other vehicles at higher speeds so you can stop safely.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, how should you position your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the side of the road.
Turn them away from the side of the road.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: Heavy smoke covers the road ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers and continue.
Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beams and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If heavy smoke covers the road, slow down immediately, move to the right, and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Smoke can harm your eyes and lungs and is dangerous to drive through.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Start slowing down when you see this warning sign.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles.
Down the middle between both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between both sides.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer down the middle. This keeps you away from both hazards.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheels:

options.text: Toward the curb.
Away from the curb.
Straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or when parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road.
